_readme: Magic, played rather than unit-tested: the Magic command, an attack spell, a heal, a
refusal the purse causes, and the swing that finishes the job anyway.
The refusal is the leg that could not be written any other way. BattleLogic proves that
a cast beyond the MP is refused; only a played fight proves the player can still DO
something afterwards - that the refusal costs no turn, leaves the page up, and lets a
cancel back out onto a command that works. A rule that stranded the player there would
pass every unit test in the file.
The numbers are exact and deterministic: 8 MP at level 1, Ember costs 3, Mend costs 4,
so the second Ember is one point short.
MP IS ONLY ASSERTED AT THE END, and that is not laziness. A fight is pure and writes
nothing until it finishes - the spend is a collected effect, applied by the world when
the battle closes - so a mid-fight assert_mp reads GameState and always answers 8. It
looks exactly like a cast that silently did not happen, which cost an hour here.
Since M29 the party is two and the fight is a pair, which changes the SHAPE of every
choice: Ember aims at ONE foe, so its confirm opens the foe cursor the way a swing does,
and Mend aims at an ally, so its confirm opens the party cursor. Rook takes a turn
between the leader's, and both slinks answer behind their own defend cues.

steps.text: the warden opens the game - hear her out first
a player who has never fought is filled in from the curve, magic included - 8 at level 1
fetch Rook - the west road will not open alone. South to the well, west to the wall, south to her.
north up the wall and through the west door, then south and west into the pair in the gap
Rows: Attack, Magic, Item, Flee. Magic is the second, so one down then confirm. The spell page is what the player has REACHED: Ember and Mend at level 1, and no Lull or Gale, which arrive at 2.

Ember first: 3 MP, and its damage ignores a slink's armour. It aims at ONE, so with a pair in front of us it opens the foe cursor exactly as a swing does - the confirm after this one is which slink burns.
and the turn passes to Rook, who just swings - Attack, then which one
then both slinks take a turn, each behind its own defend cue
hurt now, so Mend: 4 MP, which leaves one - not enough for anything. A heal aims at an ALLY, so its confirm opens the party cursor rather than the foe one.
Rook again, and the pair again
and now the leg this script exists for: one point short of an Ember. The cast is refused, it is SAID, and it costs no turn - so backing out onto Attack has to still be there to do.
out of the spells, back up onto Attack, and finish it with swings
8 - 3 - 4 = 1, and the refused cast took nothing. A fight that charged for the refusal would say 0 here, and one that never spent anything would say 8.
and the pair's ten xp is still short of the doubled curve's twenty, so nothing levelled and nothing refilled the magic on the way out
